title: Fort Dundas

groundCutout.basis: The historic ditch is defined by the documented timber enclosure and a local terrain substitution. The original field continues around its rim.

terrainReference.basis: The original 30 m Copernicus GLO-30 field at the mapped fort ruin point provides the datum. A local surface model represents the historic ditch.

mapIdentity.provider: Mapped Fort Dundas ruins and the 1824 survey narrative

identities.name: Fort Dundas
identities.address: Barlow Point, Melville Island, Northern Territory, Australia

mapIdentity.scope: OpenStreetMap ruin node 6758627778 and Northern Territory Heritage Place 12939 locate the fort. The 75 by 50 yard enclosure follows the printed report. The archaeological survey confirms an approximately 80 by 60 m extent including its projections.

note: The 1827 volume reproduces the original view made from Garden Point in 1824 and describes the felled-log wall, three-metre ditch, officers’ quarters and rush-thatched huts.
